caveats.statement: financial_facts contains multiple fact_name variants for the same economic concept (e.g., Revenues vs RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), so filtering on a single fact_name may miss entities.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_name, COUNT(DISTINCT cik) FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name LIKE '%Revenue%' GROUP BY fact_name ORDER BY 2 DESC;

caveats.statement: financial_facts may contain restated values for the same fact_name, fiscal_year, and fiscal_period across different accession_numbers, causing double counting if not deduplicated.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, COUNT(DISTINCT accession_number) FROM financial_facts GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT accession_number) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: Some companies report under IFRS (fact_category = 'ifrs-full') rather than US GAAP, so fact_name values differ and may be missed by us-gaap filters.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_category, COUNT(DISTINCT cik) FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fact_category;

caveats.statement: company_tickers may have multiple tickers per cik or missing tickers, so joining on ticker can drop or duplicate companies.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) FROM company_tickers GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: filings.form values include amendments (e.g., '10-K/A') that may duplicate the original filing's data.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT form, COUNT(*) FROM filings WHERE form LIKE '%/A' GROUP BY form;

caveats.statement: financial_facts.fiscal_period values include both annual (FY) and quarterly (Q1-Q4) periods, so mixing them without filtering causes inconsistent comparisons.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fiscal_period, COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fiscal_period;

caveats.statement: financial_facts contains multiple fact_name variants for the same economic concept (e.g., Revenues vs RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax vs SalesRevenueNet), so filtering on a single fact_name will undercount companies and periods.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_name, COUNT(DISTINCT cik) AS cik_count FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') GROUP BY fact_name ORDER BY cik_count DESC;

caveats.statement: financial_facts mixes annual (FY) and quarterly (Q1-Q4) periods in the same table, so summing fact_value without filtering fiscal_period will double-count or mix time granularities.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fiscal_period, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fiscal_period ORDER BY row_count DESC;

caveats.statement: financial_facts includes restated and original values across multiple accession_numbers for the same period, so selecting the latest filed_date per period is required to avoid stale or duplicate values.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, COUNT(DISTINCT accession_number) AS filing_count FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name = 'Revenues' GROUP BY cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period HAVING filing_count > 1 LIMIT 20;

caveats.statement: financial_facts contains both us-gaap and ifrs-full fact_category values, so mixing categories without filtering fact_category can combine incompatible accounting bases.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_category, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fact_category ORDER BY row_count DESC;

caveats.statement: financial_facts has dimension_segment and dimension_geography columns that are often NULL for consolidated totals, so filtering on dimensions without handling NULLs will exclude consolidated figures.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN dimension_segment IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_segment, SUM(CASE WHEN dimension_geography IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_geography FROM financial_facts;

caveats.statement: companies.sic_description and companies.category are free-text or loosely standardized, so grouping by them without normalization will fragment similar companies across many labels.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT sic_description, COUNT(*) AS company_count FROM companies GROUP BY sic_description ORDER BY company_count DESC LIMIT 20;

caveats.statement: company_tickers can have multiple tickers per cik and multiple exchanges, so joining companies to company_tickers without deduplication will multiply rows.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) AS ticker_count FROM company_tickers GROUP BY cik HAVING ticker_count > 1 LIMIT 20;

caveats.statement: financial_facts.fact_value is stored as text/numeric with mixed units (USD, shares, pure), so aggregating across units without filtering unit produces meaningless sums.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT unit, COUNT(*) AS row_count FROM financial_facts GROUP BY unit ORDER BY row_count DESC;

caveats.statement: companies.former_names is a JSON array, so string matching on the name column will miss companies that changed names and are referenced by their former name.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS companies_with_former_names FROM companies WHERE former_names IS NOT NULL AND former_names != '[]';

caveats.statement: Financial facts may be reported for multiple fiscal periods and forms, so the same fact_name can have multiple values per cik and end_date; always filter by fiscal_period and form_type to avoid double counting.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM financial_facts GROUP BY cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: Financial facts may have NULL or zero values for certain periods, which can skew growth rates and ratios; filter out NULLs and zeros when computing derived metrics.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_value IS NULL OR fact_value = 0;

caveats.statement: Financial facts with dimension_segment or dimension_geography set represent disaggregated data; aggregating them with consolidated totals will double count.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts WHERE dimension_segment IS NOT NULL OR dimension_geography IS NOT NULL;

caveats.statement: The same fact_name may appear under different fact_category values (us-gaap, ifrs-full, dei), so filtering by fact_category is needed for consistent comparisons.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_name, COUNT(DISTINCT fact_category) FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fact_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fact_category) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: Company tickers may have multiple exchanges or tickers per cik, so deduplication or filtering by exchange is needed when joining.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) FROM company_tickers GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: financial_facts contains multiple fact_name variants for the same economic concept (e.g., Revenues vs RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax), so filtering on a single fact_name may miss data.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fact_name, COUNT(DISTINCT cik) AS cik_count FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name IN ('Revenues','RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax','SalesRevenueNet') GROUP BY fact_name;

caveats.statement: financial_facts may contain restated or duplicate values for the same fact_name, cik, fiscal_year and fiscal_period due to multiple filings; the latest filed_date should be used.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM financial_facts GROUP BY cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: companies.category may have NULL or inconsistent values, affecting grouping by company type.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) FROM companies GROUP BY category;

caveats.statement: company_tickers may have multiple tickers per cik or missing tickers, so joining on ticker can duplicate or drop rows.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) AS ticker_count FROM company_tickers GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: financial_facts.fiscal_period values may be inconsistent (e.g., 'FY' vs 'Q4') across companies, complicating period comparisons.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT fiscal_period, COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts GROUP BY fiscal_period;

caveats.statement: company_addresses may have multiple addresses per cik, so aggregations by country or state can overcount companies.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) AS addr_count FROM company_addresses GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10;

caveats.statement: filings.form values include many form types; filtering only on '10-K' or '10-Q' may miss relevant disclosures in other forms (e.g., 8-K).
caveats.check_sql: SELECT form, COUNT(*) FROM filings GROUP BY form ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 20;

caveats.statement: financial_facts.dimension_segment and dimension_geography may be NULL for consolidated totals, so summing all rows can double-count segment-level data.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts WHERE dimension_segment IS NOT NULL OR dimension_geography IS NOT NULL;

caveats.statement: Financial facts may have multiple entries for the same fact_name, cik, fiscal_year, and fiscal_period due to restatements or different accession numbers, causing double-counting if not deduplicated.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM financial_facts GROUP BY cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10

caveats.statement: Some financial facts have NULL or zero values for fact_value, which can skew averages and ratios.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_value IS NULL OR fact_value = 0

caveats.statement: Revenue and other facts may be reported with different units (USD, shares, etc.), so mixing units in aggregations produces incorrect results.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT DISTINCT unit FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name IN ('Revenues','NetIncomeLoss')

caveats.statement: Fiscal year and fiscal period may not align with calendar year, especially for companies with non-December fiscal year ends.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fiscal_year_end FROM companies WHERE fiscal_year_end != '12-31' LIMIT 10

caveats.statement: Some companies report under different fact_category (us-gaap, ifrs-full, dei), so filtering by fact_name alone may miss or mix accounting standards.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT DISTINCT fact_category FROM financial_facts WHERE fact_name IN ('Revenues','Assets')

caveats.statement: Company tickers and exchanges may have multiple entries per cik, and some companies may have no ticker, affecting joins and market data analysis.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, COUNT(*) as ticker_count FROM company_tickers GROUP BY cik HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 LIMIT 10

caveats.statement: Financial facts may be reported for different accession numbers and filed dates, so using the latest filed_date is necessary to get the most recent restated values.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period, MAX(filed_date) as latest_filed FROM financial_facts GROUP BY cik, fact_name, fiscal_year, fiscal_period LIMIT 10

caveats.statement: Some companies may have missing or incomplete financial facts for certain periods, leading to gaps in trend analysis.
caveats.check_sql: SELECT cik, fiscal_year, COUNT(DISTINCT fact_name) as fact_count FROM financial_facts GROUP BY cik, fiscal_year HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT fact_name) < 5 LIMIT 10
